And the relief is temporal only, it does not alter classification: the system remains high-risk if it falls within a listed Annex III use-case under one of the eight areas (Article 6(2), Annex III) or satisfies both Annex I conditions under the product route (Article 6(1)). If you instead take the view that it is not high-risk under the Article 6(3) derogation, that assessment had to be documented before the system was placed on the market and carries the Article 49(2) registration obligation, with the documentation to be produced on request of national competent authorities (Article 6(4)). Practically, treat the grandfathering as fragile: the unresolved condition is whether any planned update after 2 August 2026 amounts to a "significant change in design", which is the single trigger that converts the operator's position from grandfathered to full retrofit.

Article 13 imposes no obligation to give the rejected applicant reasons for the loan denial. Its transparency duty runs exclusively to the deployer, not to the affected natural person: a credit-scoring system of this kind is high-risk under Annex III, point 5(b), and Article 13(1) requires only that it be designed and developed so that its operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret its output and use it appropriately, with an appropriate type and degree of transparency ensured with a view to compliance with the provider's and deployer's own obligations. Article 13(2) requires the system to be accompanied by instructions for use, in an appropriate digital format or otherwise, containing concise, complete, correct and clear information that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers. The Article 13(3) instructions must contain, in full: (a) the provider's identity and contact details; (b) the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance, comprising (i) the intended purpose, (ii) the level of accuracy including metrics, robustness and cybersecurity under Article 15 against which the system was tested and validated and any known or foreseeable circumstances affecting that expected level, (iii) any known or foreseeable circumstance, under intended-purpose use or reasonably foreseeable misuse, that may lead to risks to health and safety or fundamental rights referred to in Article 9(2), (iv) where applicable, the technical capabilities and characteristics of the system to provide information relevant to explain its output, (v) when appropriate, performance regarding specific persons or groups on which the system is intended to be used, (vi) when appropriate, specifications for input data or other information on the training, validation and testing data sets, and (vii) where applicable, information enabling deployers to interpret the output and use it appropriately; (c) changes to the system and its performance pre-determined by the provider; (d) the human oversight measures; (e) the computational and hardware resources needed; and (f) where relevant, a description of the log mechanisms allowing deployers to collect, store and interpret logs in accordance with Article 12. Points (iv) and (vii) are the closest Article 13 comes to explanation, but they are explanatory material supplied to you as deployer, conditioned on "where applicable", and are not a duty owed to the applicant. The individual-facing duty in the supplied corpus is Article 26(11): as a deployer of an Annex III high-risk system making or assisting decisions relating to natural persons, the operator must inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, a notification duty, not a statement of reasons, and this applies without prejudice to Article 50. Article 50(6) further confirms that Articles 50(1), (4) do not affect the Chapter III requirements and are without prejudice to other transparency obligations for deployers laid down in Union or national law, so any duty to give the applicant the grounds for the denial must be sourced outside Article 13. The operator's remaining deployer duties are to use the system in accordance with the instructions for use under Article 26(1), to assign human oversight to competent, trained natural persons under Article 26(2), and to monitor operation and retain the automatically generated logs for at least six months under Articles 26(5) and 26(6); as a financial institution subject to internal-governance requirements under Union financial services law, you satisfy those monitoring and log-retention obligations by complying with those internal-governance rules.

A separate legal or natural person established in the Union, appointed by the US parent under written mandate, must play that role, the absence of any EU establishment is precisely the trigger for Article 22(1), which requires providers established in third countries to appoint, prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, an authorised representative established in the Union. The role cannot be performed by the US parent itself or by any of its non-EU entities; it can be filled by an EU-established affiliate, or by an unrelated EU entity (including an importer or distributor acting in that additional capacity), provided it holds the written mandate. The US parent remains the provider and retains all provider obligations, Articles 9 to 15, 17, 43, 47, 48, 49, 72 and 73, since the mandate transfers tasks, not provider status; the parent must also enable the representative to perform the tasks specified in the mandate (Article 22(2)). The mandate must empower the representative to perform at least the tasks in Article 22(3): (a) verify that the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation have been drawn up and that an appropriate conformity assessment procedure was carried out by the provider; (b) keep at the disposal of the competent authorities and national authorities or bodies, for 10 years after the system's placing on the market or putting into service, the contact details of the provider, a copy of the EU declaration of conformity, the technical documentation and, where applicable, the notified body's certificate; (c) provide a competent authority, upon a reasoned request, with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity, including access to the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system to the extent those logs are under the provider's control; (d) cooperate with competent authorities, upon a reasoned request, on any action they take in relation to the system, in particular to reduce and mitigate the risks it poses; and (e) where applicable, comply with the registration obligations of Article 49(1), or, where the provider registers itself, ensure that the information in point 3 of Section A of Annex VIII is correct. The mandate must also empower the representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities on all compliance issues. Registration in the EU database may accordingly be carried out by the representative, both for Annex III high-risk systems (Article 49(1)) and for systems the provider has concluded are not high-risk under Article 6(3) (Article 49(2)). The representative's identity and contact details must appear in the instructions for use (Article 13(3)(a)) and in the EU declaration of conformity (Annex V). Finally, under Article 22(4) the representative must terminate the mandate if it considers, or has reason to consider, that the provider is acting contrary to its obligations under the Regulation, and must then immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority and, where applicable, the relevant notified body of the termination and its reasons.
